reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Acute Lateral Ankle Sprain (injury to anterior talofibular ligament), differential includes fibular fracture. severe lateral ankle pain, swelling, and bruising after twisting foot playing basketball. 28M reports twisting his right ankle inward (inversion injury) while landing from a rebound in basketball 4 hours ago. Ankle is swollen, bruised, and painful to walk on.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Acute Lateral Ankle Sprain (injury to anterior talofibular ligament), differential includes fibular fracture.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Acute Lateral Ankle Sprain (injury to anterior talofibular ligament), differential includes fibular fracture.
reference_soap.plan: Document skin integrity and distal pulses, capillary refill, sensation, and motor function. Use the Ottawa Ankle Rules to determine whether radiographs are indicated before treating this as a sprain. If fracture and neurovascular injury are excluded, use protection/compression, elevation, and progressive weight bearing as tolerated with a brace and follow-up. Escalate immediately for deformity, open injury, a pale/cool foot, new numbness/weakness, or pain and tense swelling out of proportion.

history.answer: I twisted my right ankle playing basketball about four hours ago, and now it is swollen and hurts to walk on.
The pain is on the outer side of my right ankle, right in front of the ankle bone. Only that single joint hurts.
It happened suddenly four hours ago when I landed awkwardly from a rebound during a basketball game.
It is a sharp, throbbing ache that stays around a 6 out of 10 when resting, but spikes to an 8 if I try to step on it.
Yes, the outer ankle swelled up within an hour after the twist, and I can see some purple bruising spreading, though it is not hot to the touch.
No, I have never had morning stiffness in my ankles or any other joints.
Putting weight on the foot or bending the ankle inward makes it much worse, while keeping it elevated and resting makes it feel better.
I was able to limp off the court right after it happened, and I can take four steps if I really limp, though it hurts.
I jumped up for a rebound and landed directly on another player's foot, rolling my right ankle inward. I felt a distinct pop when it turned.
The tenderness is right in the soft depression just in front of the outer ankle bone. The bone itself does not hurt when I press it.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/76 mmHg, pulse 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-developed young male sitting comfortably on the examination table with the right leg resting on a stool, showing mild discomfort when repositioning the foot.

Moderate localized swelling and ecchymosis over the right anterolateral ankle with marked tenderness over the anterior talofibular ligament; no tenderness over the posterior edge or tip of the lateral or medial malleolus, base of the fifth metatarsal, or navicular bone; left ankle and all other joints appear normal without effusion or tenderness.
Both calves are symmetric and soft without tenderness; Achilles tendons are intact bilaterally with normal resting tension and negative Thompson squeeze test.
Antalgic limp favoring the right side; able to take four consecutive steps bearing weight on the right foot with moderate discomfort.
Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are 2+ bilaterally, and capillary refill time is under two seconds in all toes.
Light touch and pinprick sensation are fully intact across the distributions of the superficial peroneal, deep peroneal, sural, saphenous, and tibial nerves.
Great toe extension, ankle plantar flexion, and dorsiflexion are 5/5 bilaterally, with active right ankle inversion and eversion slightly guarded due to discomfort.
No open lacerations, skin breakdown, or tenting; no rashes, nail changes, or tophaceous deposits.
